points.quote: Use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is permitted provided that such use is clearly identified and referenced.
points.anchor: How AI may be used at HW
points.gist: Generative AI use is permitted as long as it is clearly identified and referenced.

points.quote: Generative AI spelling and grammar checking (e.g. MS Word, Grammarly) does not need to be referenced unless specifically indicated within the course.
points.anchor: How AI may be used at HW
points.gist: Spelling and grammar checking with tools such as MS Word or Grammarly need not be referenced unless the course says so.

points.quote: Only use GAI if it is permitted on your course and only use if for the purposes it is permitted e.g. you might be permitted to use it to research a topic but not to help you write it up.
points.anchor: How to choose whether to use generative AI
points.gist: Use GAI only if the course permits it and only for the permitted purposes, for example research but not writing up.

points.quote: Using artificial intelligence to complete a whole assignment for you would not be acting with academic integrity, as you would be presenting work that
points.gist: Using AI to complete a whole assignment is not academic integrity because the work would not be your own.

points.quote: This is plagiarism and would be considered academic misconduct.
points.gist: Presenting AI-completed work as your own is plagiarism and academic misconduct.

points.quote: HW will not be utilising any generative AI detection tools for the period of AY23-24.
points.anchor: How AI may be used at HW
points.gist: HW will not use generative AI detection tools during AY23-24.

points.quote: Keep copies of your prompts and outputs for future reference. You may need to provide copies of them in your assignments.
points.gist: Keep copies of prompts and outputs, as you may have to supply them in assignments.

points.quote: Where the output contributes to summative assessment, you must ensure that you reference this following the referencing style and any specific guidance from your course.
points.anchor: How you use the output from generative AI
points.gist: If AI output contributes to summative assessment, it must be referenced in the course's referencing style.

points.quote: AI generated content may not be accurate (even where it includes references), the outputs are predictions, they are not facts, and the content may be based on biased or stereotypical perspectives.
points.anchor: How to interpret the output from generative AI
points.gist: AI content may be inaccurate even with references; outputs are predictions, not facts, and may be biased or stereotypical.

points.quote: As you cross-check the content, look for sources that are Accurate, Current, Objective, Relevant and Named.
points.anchor: How to interpret the output from generative AI
points.gist: When cross-checking, look for sources that are Accurate, Current, Objective, Relevant and Named (ACORN).

points.quote: Copying this output may be a breach of copyright, so try to identify and use the original source, ensuring you comply with copyright as you do so.
points.anchor: How to interpret the output from generative AI
points.gist: Copying AI output may breach copyright, so identify and use the original source.

points.quote: It is not good practice to use the whole assessment question or brief as a prompt.
points.anchor: How to write a generative AI prompt
points.gist: It is not good practice to use the whole assessment question or brief as a prompt.

points.quote: Write an essay plan for a critical evaluation of the impact of climate change in my country on food production by farmers.
points.anchor: How to write a generative AI prompt
points.gist: A worked example shows a vague climate change prompt refined into a specific essay-plan request.

points.quote: Students should use HW supported technology as this has been reviewed to ensure that it protects their privacy, is cyber secure and is safe to use.
points.gist: Students should use HW supported technology, which has been reviewed for privacy, cyber security and safety.

points.quote: If it is a requirement of your course, and you have concerns about using AI, you should raise this with your course leader clearly explaining your concerns.
points.anchor: How to choose whether to use generative AI
points.gist: If AI use is required and you have concerns, raise them with your course leader.
